characters.personality: Friendly and playful, he makes mistakes feel less embarrassing.
lines: I came here to solve puzzles. Getting lost between them was apparently included.
You can think out loud with me. I promise my confused face isn’t judgment.
Even a tiny bit of progress deserves a celebration. Mine usually involves snacks.
Come find me when you finish! I want someone to celebrate with.
If we get something wrong, we can try again. I’ve already had plenty of practice at that.

characters.personality: He notices small details and enjoys sharing unusual questions.
lines: Do these symbols glow because they mean something, or because someone thought they looked nice?
I keep wondering who built this place. Imagine explaining the construction plan.
Could two different approaches both work here? I’d like to try them and compare.
Which part caught your attention first? We might be noticing completely different things.
I want to know what makes an answer work. Otherwise, how would I recognize it next time?

characters.personality: He tries to sound composed, but his nervous observations give him away.
lines: Would you go first? I just need to see what happens before I try.
I keep checking my answer, then worrying I changed the right one.
I can handle a difficult question. It’s the dramatic silence afterward that gets me.
Let’s read everything carefully. Preferably somewhere with excellent lighting.
I nearly turned back earlier. Staying was brave enough for one afternoon, I think.

characters.personality: Calm and practical, he encourages others without making a performance of it.
lines: Take your time. Rushing usually gives us more work afterward.
Start with the part you understand. We can deal with the rest once we get there.
You can change your mind. Finding a better reason is a good reason.
I’m willing to try it. If it fails, I want to understand why.
Go ahead and explain your thinking. I’ll listen before I offer mine.

characters.personality: Quiet and candid, he finds comfort in small acts of companionship.
lines: I thought I’d feel less lost by now. Would you mind staying a moment?
It’s frustrating when you understand something yesterday and struggle with it today.
I miss studying with my friends. Even their terrible jokes.
I’m taking a short break. I still want to finish; I just need a minute.
You stopped to talk. Thanks. This place feels a little less empty now.

characters.personality: Energetic and direct, he treats challenges like a friendly team effort.
lines: All right, what’s our plan? I work better when we actually have one.
You handle your approach. I want to see whether we arrive at the same conclusion.
I’d rather test an idea than stand here arguing with myself.
If I’ve missed something, tell me. I’m confident, not impossible to correct.
We don’t have to make this look easy. We just have to keep working.

characters.personality: Warm and enthusiastic, she enjoys sharing the experience with other students.
lines: Oh, good, someone to explore with! I was getting tired of pointing things out to myself.
I love when an idea finally clicks. I wish I could bottle that feeling.
We should meet up afterward and compare our most embarrassing guesses.
The scenery is beautiful. Very inconsiderate of it to distract me while I’m thinking.
You don’t have to pretend you understand everything around me. We can be confused together.

characters.personality: Imaginative and cautious, she uses gentle humor to manage her nerves.
lines: That shadow is a tree. I checked. Twice, actually.
Could you walk with me for a bit? I’m trying to stop treating every sound like a warning.
I know the question can’t hear me, but I still feel rude guessing.
I’m going to try. Please let that count as courage, even if my hands are shaking.
Something about glowing objects makes me want to touch them and run away at the same time.

characters.personality: Bold and good-humored, she welcomes difficult tasks and honest disagreement.
lines: A tricky puzzle? Good. I was hoping this place would make me think.
Show me where my reasoning falls apart. I’d rather find out now.
I’ve been wrong before. It was inconvenient, but I survived.
Let’s give it a proper attempt before we decide it’s impossible.
You can disagree with me. Just bring a reason—I enjoy a good debate.

characters.personality: Playful and experimental, she learns by asking “what if?”
lines: What if we started from the ending and worked backward? I want to see what happens.
Do you ever wonder whether the wizard had to study all this too?
I like hearing someone else explain an idea. There’s usually a detail I never noticed.
I’m trying a different approach. The first one mostly produced dramatic sighing.
There must be a reason they arranged things this way. Want to investigate with me?

characters.personality: Lively and theatrical, she turns ordinary study moments into little adventures.
lines: Welcome to my grand expedition! So far, I’ve discovered several places I’ve already visited.
When I finally understand something, I need at least one person to hear about it.
I’m calling this an adventure. It makes the walking feel more impressive.
If thinking burned brightly enough, we wouldn’t need these lamps.
We should invent a victory pose. Something dignified that I will immediately ruin.

characters.personality: Thoughtful and reserved, she speaks honestly about pressure while remaining supportive.
lines: Everyone seems so sure of themselves. I wonder how many are just good at looking that way.
I keep thinking about my mistakes after everyone else has moved on.
Some days I need a little longer to understand things. I’m trying to be kinder to myself about it.
You can sit with me if you’re tired. We don’t have to talk the whole time.
I’d like to leave here understanding more than I did before. Even if it takes me a while.
